# ECC Bridge Boundaries

- Treat ECC as an attached system first. Before editing bridge surfaces, classify the work as one of: delegated runtime, shared MCP surface, standalone utility app, thin sidecar adapter, or curated workflow import.
- Keep OpenSpace as the control plane. Registry ownership stays in [openspace/config/external_agents.json](../../openspace/config/external_agents.json), [openspace/config/standalone_apps.json](../../openspace/config/standalone_apps.json), [openspace/mcp_server.py](../../openspace/mcp_server.py), and dashboard APIs; do not mirror ECC's full command, agent, hook, or state-store surfaces inside OpenSpace unless the user explicitly asks for that duplication.
- Prefer existing contracts over new protocol code. Try `http-json`, `openai-compat`, `chat-thread`, or shared MCP first. Reach for [openspace/openhuman_gateway.py](../../openspace/openhuman_gateway.py) or [openspace/openhuman_rpc_gateway.py](../../openspace/openhuman_rpc_gateway.py) patterns only when ECC truly needs status-aware RPC or a protocol-specific adapter.
- Deep-link ECC UI before rebuilding it. If ECC already exposes a dashboard or operator surface, prefer a card in [openspace/config/standalone_apps.json](../../openspace/config/standalone_apps.json) and existing frontend consumers over duplicating ECC's catalog or session view in OpenSpace.
- If the request is about reusing ECC workflow ideas, translate selected workflows into OpenSpace host skills, prompts, or instructions instead of copying the full ECC command tree, hook runtime, or harness installation assets. Keep the translated surface in OpenSpace terms and link back to source docs when attribution or further reading helps.
- Any bridge change that affects ids, env names, ports, Compose, dashboard cards, or docs must move together across config, backend, frontend, docs, and smoke coverage. Do not land a half-registered ECC surface.
- When introducing or changing an adapter contract, document the concrete endpoint inventory first: base URL, health or status URL, action or handoff URL, auth method, request and response schema, timeout or retry expectations, and history or session model. If the ECC contract cannot be verified from source evidence, stop and report the gap instead of inventing it.
- Keep env naming explicit and product-scoped. Prefer `ECC_*` names when the dependency is ECC-owned, and update `.env*`, frontend env defaults, Compose, and install docs together when those names become user-facing.
- Preserve existing OpenSpace dashboard semantics. If a new ECC surface is only browseable, model it as a standalone app; if it accepts work, model it as an external agent or MCP surface; if it does both, keep those responsibilities distinct in config and docs.
- Validate the smallest touched slice: JSON shape for registries, targeted tests for backend or dashboard wiring, `docker compose config` for Compose changes, and `smoke_test_mcp.py` when the new surface is meant to be user-visible.
- Explicit non-goals for ECC bridge work: vendoring the ECC repo into OpenSpace, duplicating ECC's hook runtime, creating a second control plane in the dashboard, or promising automatic import of every ECC command, agent, or workflow.
